Sebta et Melilla : les pointillés de Google Maps qui fâchent l'Espagne

2026-08-03 Bladi.net Google Maps, Sebta, Melilla, disputed borders, dashed lines, territorial claims, Morocco, Spain, cartographic representation, border disputes
Read the source article

Quick summary

Google Maps uses dashed lines for the borders of Sebta (Ceuta) and Melilla — the symbol reserved for disputed territorial limits — giving global visibility to Morocco's claim over the Spanish-held cities and reigniting debate in Spain.

Key takeaways

  • Google Maps displays the borders of Sebta and Melilla as dashed lines, the platform's convention for borders where parties haven't agreed on the boundary
  • The representation was visible as early as 2020 and caused controversy in 2023 when the Observatory of Sebta and Melilla contested Google's cartographic choice
  • Madrid considers both cities as fully Spanish territory; Morocco claims them as occupied territories that should return to the Kingdom's territorial integrity
  • Spanish maps typically show the separation from Morocco as a normal, definitively established international border
  • Google has not specified the exact date this treatment was applied nor why the two cities are classified as disputed
